applies_to: early warning for slender unrestrained beams
applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: Uses public UK/Eurocode-oriented guidance plus an open-access LTB article; not a design procedure.

claims.text: A laterally unrestrained steel member in major-axis bending can be governed by lateral-torsional buckling rather than only cross-section bending resistance.
Sufficient restraint to the compression flange can remove lateral-torsional buckling as a governing susceptibility for a beam check.

source_refs.locator: Lateral Torsional Buckling of Steel Beams Elastically Restrained at the Support Nodes

claims.text: Restraint stiffness and restraint location can materially affect lateral-torsional buckling behavior, so Fraia should not collapse restraint into a simple yes/no tag when better data is available.

limitations: No LTB formula or reduction factor is encoded in this card.
Applicable standards and national annexes must be selected before any LTB design check.

summary: Lateral-torsional buckling is a restraint-sensitive steel beam stability mode that must remain separate from simple cross-section bending capacity.
